Read the following statements regarding India's SHAKTI-based aerospace semiconductor chip in February 2025 and choose the correct option from the below.
Statement 1: In February 2025, IIT Delhi and ISRO jointly developed and booted an indigenous SHAKTI-based aerospace-grade semiconductor chip. Statement 2: The chip is based on the open-source RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture under the DIRV initiative of MeitY.
x: The Feb 2025 SHAKTI-based aerospace chip (IRIS) was developed and booted by IIT Madras with ISRO – not IIT Delhi – so Statement 1 is wrong. It is built on the open-source RISC-V ISA, the basis of MeitY's DIR-V programme, so Statement 2 is right.

s: Which one of the following pairs of semiconductor plants in India and their locations is not correctly matched? Semiconductor Plant Location
o: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test Pvt. Ltd. Assam
HCL-Foxconn Joint Venture India Chip Ltd.
x: HCL–Foxconn's JV India Chip Pvt. Ltd. is at Jewar, Uttar Pradesh (near Noida International Airport), not in the state the question pairs it with. CG Power (Sanand, Gujarat), Tata's OSAT (Assam) and SiCSem (Odisha) are correctly matched. (The printed options have lost their location column.)

s: Which company makes the fighter aircraft 'Rafale'?
x: The Rafale is made by France's Dassault Aviation (India: 36 in service, 114 more approved in 2026). Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman are US firms; Hawker Beechcraft made trainers/business aircraft.

With reference to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), consider the following statements:
1. All types of UAVs can do vertical landing.
2. All types of UAVs can do automated hovering.
3. All types of UAVs can use battery only as a source of power supply.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: None is correct: only VTOL/multirotor UAVs can land vertically or hover – fixed-wing UAVs need runways or launch/recovery systems and forward motion; many UAVs use fuel engines, hybrids or solar power, not only batteries.

Consider the following statements with respect to the AI Impact Summit, 2026 held in New Delhi:
1. The Summit's intellectual framework was based on three foundational Sutras: People, Planning, and Progress.
2. The Preamble of the Summit stresses Democratising AI Resources, which acknowledges the Charter for Democratic Diffusion of AI as a binding framework to support locally relevant innovation and strengthen resilient AI ecosystems while respecting national laws.
3. The New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact was structured around seven Chakras (Pillars), which included Access for Social Empowerment, AI for Science, and Secure and Trusted AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 3 is correct: the New Delhi Declaration was built on seven Chakras (pillars) incl. Access for Social Empowerment, AI for Science and Secure & Trusted AI. 1 is wrong – the Sutras are People, Planet and Progress (not Planning); 2 is wrong – the Charter for Democratic Diffusion of AI is voluntary and non-binding.

Consider the following statements:
1.
Statement I: Some rare earth elements are used in the manufacture of flat television screens and computer monitors.
2. Statement II: Some rare earth elements have phosphorescent properties. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct, but Statement II is correct
x: Both are true and II explains I: rare-earths such as europium, terbium and yttrium are phosphors – their phosphorescent emission gives the colours of flat-screen TVs and monitors.
